name: Bahadur Shah II
role: Last Mughal emperor and symbolic leader of 1857
contribution: Bahadur Shah II, the last Mughal emperor, was proclaimed the symbolic sovereign of the 1857 rebellion after rebel forces entered Delhi.
context: His court provided the rebellion with an imperial symbol, while military command remained divided among regional commanders such as Bakht Khan. After the British recaptured Delhi, Bahadur Shah was tried and exiled to Rangoon.
impact: His brief restoration as a rebel symbol linked the uprising to the memory and legitimacy of the Mughal Empire. The episode also shows the gap between symbolic authority and coordinated military power in 1857.
highlight: Last Mughal emperor and symbolic sovereign of the 1857 rebellion in Delhi.
seoTitle: Bahadur Shah II: Symbolic Leader of the 1857 Rebellion
seoDescription: Learn about Bahadur Shah II, the last Mughal emperor who became the symbolic leader of the 1857 rebellion in Delhi.
shortAnswer: Bahadur Shah II was the last Mughal emperor and symbolic sovereign proclaimed by rebel forces in Delhi during 1857.
alternateNames: Abu Zafar Sirajuddin Muhammad Bahadur Shah

faq.question: What was Bahadur Shah II's role in 1857?
faq.answer: Rebel forces in Delhi proclaimed him their symbolic sovereign, linking the uprising to Mughal legitimacy even though military command was divided.
